doc.title: Richard Wyands interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: A lifetime as a musician and the tough years
summary: He never held another career job; the first New York year and slow mid-60s led him to tour with Burrell.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: You’ve gone through your whole life as a musician. That’s saying something.

I’ve never done anything else, since I was in high school. I had some jobs that I did, summer jobs. I worked at a shipyard, all sorts of factories and canneries, but this was just during the summer. I hadn’t planned on doing that forever. But I haven’t done anything else since. Nothing. I got kind of close, though, I thought to myself.
Yeah. Which were the tough years?

No I’m only kidding. No. The first year of course, waiting for the union to give me a break. Mid-60s I guess. I think that’s one reason why I went out on the road with Kenny Burrell, because things were kind of slow here in the city. So I decided well this will give me a chance to get to California to see your family. My mother and father were still there then, and other relatives and friends. So I’d come to California maybe twice a year, which was great. But all of that’s over with. There aren’t many clubs. Minnesota we even went to.
Wow. I hope it wasn’t in the winter.
Oh no, no winter, no, no.
